lines.text: Who tells your face to frown? It starts with one small, quiet message.
lines.phonemes: hˌuː tˈɛlz jɔː fˈeɪs tə fɹˈaʊn? ɪt stˈɑːts wɪð wˈɒn smˈɔːl, kwˈaɪət mˈɛsɪdʒ.

lines.text: Every frown begins at the end of a nerve. The nerve lets out a chemical messenger called acetylcholine. It reaches a muscle fibre, which gets the message and pulls.
lines.phonemes: ˈɛvɹɪ fɹˈaʊn bɪɡˈɪnz at ðɪ ˈɛnd əvə nˈɜːv. ðə nˈɜːv lˈɛts ˈaʊt ɐ kˈɛmɪkəl mˈɛsɪndʒə kˈɔːld ˈasɪtˌɪlkəlˌiːn. ɪt ɹˈiːtʃɪz ɐ mˈʌsəl fˈaɪbə, wˌɪtʃ ɡˈɛts ðə mˈɛsɪdʒ and pˈʊlz.

lines.text: Botulinum toxin gets inside that nerve ending. There it cuts one protein, SNAP-25, that the message needs. The message stays stuck, so the muscle gets no signal and the frown can relax.
lines.phonemes: bˌɒtjʊlˈaɪnəm tˈɒksɪn ɡˈɛts ɪnsˈaɪd ðat nˈɜːv ˈɛndɪŋ. ðeəɹ ɪt kˈʌts wˈɒn pɹˈəʊtiːn, snˈap twˈɛnti fˈaɪv , ðatðə mˈɛsɪdʒ nˈiːdz. ðə mˈɛsɪdʒ stˈeɪz stˈʌk, sˌəʊ ðə mˈʌsəl ɡˈɛts nˈəʊ sˈɪɡnəl and ðə fɹˈaʊn kan ɹɪlˈaks.

lines.text: Two hundred years ago, a German doctor named Justinus Kerner studied a poison in spoiled sausages that caused paralysis. He guessed it might one day become a medicine.
lines.phonemes: tˈuː hˈʌndɹɪd jˈiəz ɐɡˈəʊ, ɐ dʒˈɜːmən dˈɒktə nˈeɪmd jʊstˈiːnʊs kˈɛɐnɐ stˈʌdid ɐ pˈɔɪzən ɪn spˈɔɪld sˈɒsɪdʒɪz ðat kˈɔːzd pəɹˈaləsˌɪs. hiː ɡˈɛst ɪt mˌaɪt wˈɒn dˈeɪ bɪkˌʌm ɐ mˈɛdsən.

lines.text: And here is the twist. The block does not last. The nerve slowly grows new endings, and about three months later the message flows again.
lines.phonemes: and hˈiəɹ ɪz ðə twˈɪst. ðə blˈɒk dʌznˌɒt lˈast. ðə nˈɜːv slˈəʊli ɡɹˈəʊz njˈuː ˈɛndɪŋz, and ɐbˌaʊt θɹˈiː mˈʌnθs lˈeɪtə ðə mˈɛsɪdʒ flˈəʊz ɐɡˈɛn.

lines.text: So a frown is a message, and this toxin blocks it. The skin was never the target. The nerve was.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ ɐ fɹˈaʊn ɪz ɐ mˈɛsɪdʒ, and ðɪs tˈɒksɪn blˈɒks ɪt. ðə skˈɪn wɒz nˈɛvə ðə tˈɑːɡɪt. ðə nˈɜːv wɒz.

lines.text: Next: two neighbours, under the same sun, and one experiment. Which hand aged?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: tˈuː nˈeɪbəz, ˌʌndə ðə sˈeɪm sˈʌn, and wˈɒn ɛkspˈɛɹɪmənt. wˌɪtʃ hˈand ˈeɪdʒd?
